The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
3,\,6,\,12,\,24,\,…
$$

form a geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =2 \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =\frac{12}{6} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our geometric sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1}=3({2}^{n-1})=\frac{3}{2}(2)^{n}.
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
A={\frac{3}{2}(2)^{n}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}(2)^{N} & =98\,304 \\ {2}^{N} & =65\,536 \\ N & ={log}_{2}⁡(65\,536) \\ N & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(65\,536)}{{log}_{10}⁡(2)} \\ N & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={\frac{3}{2}(2)^{n}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 16}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $16$ elements, we must have $|A|=16.$
